title: Inducing and measuring apoptotic cell death in mouse pancreatic β-cells and in isolated islets
protocol: Plate MIN6 cells at a density of 5 × 10^4 cells/cm^2.
Allow cells to recover overnight (∼16 h).
Treat cells with staurosporine (1 μM), thapsigargin (1 μM), or tunicamycin (5 ng/mL) in the late afternoon of the following day.
Monitor cell death using live cell imaging with propidium iodide (PI).
Set up individual control and experimental replicates alternated on a plate for reproducibility.
Begin pretreatment with z-VADfmk or AAT 2 hours prior to adding death stimuli if applicable.
Add propidium iodide (PI) diluted 1:1000 directly to the media.
Add Hoechst 33342 diluted 1:1000 directly to the media.
Gently swirl plate to mix.
Incubate cells for 5 minutes in the dark at 37°C.
Image cells as described in the relevant protocol section.
Image a minimum of 4 fields per well to minimize technical variation.
Average values from imaged fields to represent each well accurately.
Control wells should show few propidium iodide (PI)-positive cells.
Wells treated with death inducers should display a significant increase in PI-positive cells.
Quantify dead cells by counting both PI+ Hoechst+ and PI- Hoechst+ cells.
Present data as the percentage of PI+ cells relative to total stained cells.
Cells must be imaged immediately after incubation due to toxicity from long-term exposure to Hoechst and PI.
Consider using TUNEL for detecting cell death in response to palmitate instead of propidium iodide.
If necrotic cell death is a concern, omit propidium iodide and measure condensed nuclei using Hoechst staining alone.
Culture cells directly onto 6-well tissue culture plates without further coating or use of coverslip.
Begin death treatment as described in step 1c.
Prepare 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for staining reagents.
Prepare cell permeabilization solution.
Remove 100 μl of label solution from the TUNEL reaction mixture kit and place in a separate tube for use as a negative control.
Perform a quick spin on the tube containing enzyme solution to collect all liquid contents at the bottom.
Remove 50 μl of enzyme solution from its tube and add it to the remaining 400 μl of label solution in the original tube.
Keep the TUNEL reaction mixture light-sensitive, cold, and covered from light.
Wash cells three times with 1× PBS after cell treatment completion.
Fix cells with 4% PFA for 10 minutes at 20°C.
Rinse cells with 1× PBS.
Permeabilize cells with cell permeabilization solution for 5 minutes at 20°C.
Add the prepared TUNEL solution to each sample, ensuring full coverage.
Apply label solution alone to a sample as a negative control.
Treat at least one sample with DNAse for the positive control.
Incubate cells for 1 hour in the dark at 37°C.
Cover samples to prevent drying.
Wash cells with 1× PBS for 5 minutes twice.
Wash cells with 1× PBS-T for 5 minutes once.
Place a drop of mounting media directly on top of the fixed cells in each well of the 6-well culture plate.
Place a glass coverslip carefully over the drop of mounting media to avoid creating bubbles.
Image and quantify samples for TUNEL staining as described.
Imaging can be performed up to 1 week after placing cells in the dark at 4°C before fluorescence signal fades.
Hand pick islets using a P20 pipet with a P10 tip.
Place 150-200 islets per well in a 12-well non-tissue culture treated plate.
Resuspend islets in 1 ml of culture media.
Treat islets with thapsigargin (1 μM) for 24 hours or palmitate (1.2 mM) for 3 days.
Prepare 4% PFA solution.
Collect the contents of each well containing treated islets and media into separate Eppendorf tubes using a P1000 pipet.
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 100 g at 20°C to collect the islets at the bottom of the tube.
Carefully discard supernatant and wash islets with 1 mL 1× PBS.
Fix islets by resuspending in 300 μL 4% PFA and rotate tubes for 10 minutes at 4°C.
In chemical hood, add 1 mL 1× PBS to each tube.
Centrifuge tubes for 3 minutes at 100 g.
Discard supernatant in PFA waste container.
Wash islets with 1 mL 1× PBS.
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 100 g at 20°C to collect the islets at the bottom of the tube.
Carefully discard supernatant, leaving only ∼50 μL of PBS in the tube.
Using a P200 pipet, resuspend islets and transfer to the center of a cryomold.
Wait for islets to sink to the bottom of the mold.
Flash freeze on dry ice.
While cryomold (with frozen islets) is placed on dry ice, slowly and sequentially add OCT to the mold, beginning on the outer edges, working in towards the islet.
Once the mold is fully filled with OCT, allow OCT to freeze completely.
Wrap block in foil and place in −80°C freezer.
Allow slides to acclimate to 20°C (from −80°C) for 10 minutes.
Perform TUNEL staining.
Place slides in slide holder and submerge in 1× PBS.
Wash slides in 1× PBS on shaker for 3 min.
Perform two more washes of slides in fresh 1× PBS on shaker for 3 min each.
Add previously prepared TUNEL solution dropwise to each tissue section, approximately 75 μL per slide.
Add label solution alone (without TdT) to at least one sample as a negative control.
Treat some slides with DNAseI for positive control.
Cover each slide with a rectangular coverslip.
Place slides in hydrophobic chamber and incubate for 1 h in the dark at 37°C.
Remove coverslips by vertically placing slides in container filled with 1× PBS, allowing gravity to remove them naturally.
If necessary, let the slide sit in 1× PBS for 30 s before attempting removal again gently moving the slide up and down if needed.
Do not force coverslip off manually.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 min × 2.
Wash slides with 1× PBS-T for 5 min.
Coverslip slides with mounting media containing DAPI.
Image samples.
Dissect entire pancreas from desired mouse model using the spleen to grab the tissue so that the pancreas is not damaged.
Thoroughly wash pancreas with ice-cold 1× PBS.
Place pancreas in 50 mL tube containing 5 mL 4% PFA.
Discard PFA in properly marked waste container.
Wash tissue with cold 1× PBS.
Dehydrate tissue by placing pancreatic tissue in 30% EtOH for 5 min.
Discard liquid and resubmerge tissue with 5 mL 50% EtOH for 5 min.
Discard liquid and resubmerge tissue with 5 mL 70% EtOH.
Place tissue in paraffin cassette labeled with pencil and resubmerge in 70% EtOH.
Embed pancreas in paraffin.
Using microtome, prepare 5 μm tissue sections.
Place completed slides at 20°C until ready for staining.
Bake slides at 65°C until paraffin has melted off (approximately 1–2 h).
Cool slides at 20°C for 1 h.
Heat water bath to 90°C.
Prepare antigen retrieval solution by diluting 2.5 mL Antigen unmasking solution in 250 mL of dH2O.
Preheat antigen retrieval solution to 90°C in the water bath.

Deparaffinize tissue sections by placing them in Xylene (5 min × 3 times), then in 100% EtOH (1 min × 2), followed by 95% EtOH (1 min × 2), then in 70% ETOH (1 min × 2) and finally in 1× PBS (1 min × 2).
Submerge slides in antigen retrieval solution at 90°C for 10 min.
Remove slide container from water bath and place entire container in ice to cool for 10 min.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 min.
Wash slides with 1× PBS-T for 5 min.
Prepare Enzyme Solution (Proteinase K) by diluting 100 μL of proteinase K in 900 μL of DNAse/RNAse free distilled water.
Incubate slides horizontally with enzyme solution for 15 min at 20°C.
Wash slides in 1× PBS on a shaker for 3 min.
Perform TUNEL staining.
Prepare TUNEL reagents as specified.
Place slides in new 1× PBS and perform two more washes on the shaker for 3 min each.
Add previously prepared TUNEL solution dropwise to each tissue section on the slide, approximately 75 μL per slide.
Add label solution alone (without TdT) to at least one sample as a negative control.
Treat slides with DNAseI for positive control if necessary.
Cover each slide with a coverslip to distribute TUNEL solution evenly.
Place slides in a hydrophobic chamber and incubate for 1 hour in the dark at 37°C.
Gently remove the coverslip after incubation.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 minutes × 2.
Wash slides with 1× PBS-T for 5 minutes, once.
Block slides for 1 hour at 20°C in a hydrophobic chamber using 10% goat serum diluted in 1× PBS-T.
Incubate with primary antibody (Insulin antibody made in Guinea Pig, Dako, cat# A056401-2, diluted 1:2000) for 16 hours at 4°C in the blocking solution.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 minutes × 2.
Wash slides with 1× PBS-T for 5 minutes, once.
Incubate each slide with secondary antibody (Goat anti-Guinea Pig 568, Invitrogen, cat# A-11075, diluted 1:1000 in blocking serum) for 1 hour at 20°C.
Coverslip with mounting media containing DAPI.
Image the samples.
Block slides for 1 h at 20°C in hydrophobic chamber with 10% goat serum diluted in 1× PBS-T.
Incubate with primary antibody (cleaved caspase-3 antibody made in rabbit, Cell Signaling, cat# 9661, diluted 1:100) for 16 h at 4°C.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 min × 2 and 1× PBS-T for 5 min × 1.
Incubate each slide with secondary antibody (Goat anti-Rabbit 488, Invitrogen, cat# A-11034, diluted 1:1000) for 1 h at 20°C.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 min × 2 and 1× PBS-T for 5 min × 1.
Incubate slides with insulin primary antibody (Insulin antibody made in Guinea Pig, Dako, cat# A056401-2, dilute 1:2000) for 2 h at 20°C.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 min × 2.
Wash slides with 1× PBS-T for 5 min × 1.
Incubate each slide with secondary antibody (1:1000, diluted in blocking serum) for 1 h at 20°C.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 min × 2.
Wash slides with 1× PBS-T for 5 min × 1.
Coverslip with mounting media containing DAPI (VECTASHIELD Vibrance Antifade Mounting Medium with DAPI).
Image samples.
